analysis: This PR changes documentation only. In docs/architecture/inference.md, the changed head ranges are line 3 (date) and 252-260, which are not in the supplied head excerpts. The visible units 405-1213 are unchanged context. In docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md, line 3 (date) and lines 784-791 changed. The new text says a provider-staged complete-checkpoint import creates destinations already available from host bytes, never evaluates or fences them, and so avoids waiting on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock. It also says the import plan charges the largest host-zero source as staging scratch. This documents a code change in libs/mlx-swift-lm/.../CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift (CBv2CompleteCheckpointImport) that is not supplied. Relevant threats: T-041 (encrypted SSD prefix cache, A-001) and T-010/T-029 (availability). Based on the docs alone, there is no regression: encryption, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, scope salt and KEK bindings are unchanged. Next pass should check, if the code diff exists, that (1) host bytes are decrypted and authenticated before import, (2) staging scratch stays charged to the GlobalKVCacheBudget and is released on failure or cancellation, and (3) plaintext host buffers are zeroed or released promptly (T-028 residue). Nothing here changes the threat model; the T-041 mitigations remain accurate. The code behind the claim is outside the supplied evidence, so the claim is unverified, not shown unsafe.
